label: Place
name: Dominica
summary:
Dominica, officially the Commonwealth of Dominica, is an island country in the Windward Islands of the Caribbean. The island's 71,000 people make it one of the smallest sovereign nations in the Americas. Dominica is notable for its relative preservation of Caribbean Kalinago (Island Carib) culture — the only island in the eastern Caribbean with a surviving indigenous Kalinago community, approximately 3,000 people living in the Carib Territory established in 1903.

Columbus sighted Dominica on a Sunday in November 1493 (hence the name, from the Latin for 'Sunday'). The Kalinago resisted European colonization so effectively that permanent European settlement did not succeed until the 18th century, making Dominica one of the last Caribbean islands to be colonized. Britain and France contested the island repeatedly before Britain formally acquired it in 1763. The plantation economy relied on enslaved African labor for coffee and sugar; emancipation (1834) and the subsequent decline of plantation agriculture left Dominica as one of the least economically developed British Caribbean colonies.

Dominica gained independence in 1978. It is known as the 'Nature Isle of the Caribbean' for its volcanic landscape, dense rainforest, and high rainfall — making it a significant ecotourism destination. Hurricane Maria (September 2017) devastated the island, destroying 90% of buildings and the entire agricultural sector — a catastrophe that accelerated investment in climate-resilient infrastructure and made Dominica a global case study in post-hurricane reconstruction.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Dominica's preservation of Caribbean Kalinago culture and its resistance to European colonization make it a unique case study in indigenous resilience. The island's status as the only surviving indigenous community in the eastern Caribbean has significant implications for our understanding of colonialism and cultural heritage.

causes: Kalinago resistance to colonization delaying permanent European settlement until the 18th century
French-British colonial rivalry making Dominica a contested frontier island with no stable colonial economy
British acquisition (1763) establishing a plantation economy based on enslaved African labor for coffee and cocoa
effects: Only surviving indigenous Kalinago community in the eastern Caribbean (3,000 people in the Carib Territory)
Hurricane Maria (2017) devastation — 90% of buildings destroyed, triggering a global conversation about climate resilience in small island states
Citizenship-by-investment program becoming a significant revenue source — Dominica's program among the world's most established
